Access.description: How many requests a product costs, which is what decides the schedule.
Access.title: Access

AliasCreate.description: What a source calls this attribute.
AliasCreate.title: AliasCreate

AliasKind.description:
Where an alias may be read from.

Not how confident we are — that is `origin`. This says whether the string may be
trusted outside a feed's brand field.
AliasKind.title: AliasKind

AttributeCategoryRead.description: A category an attribute is bound to, and what that category makes of it.
AttributeCategoryRead.title: AttributeCategoryRead

AttributeRef.description: The attribute a binding is of, as a table row needs it.
AttributeRef.title: AttributeRef

AttributeRow.description: An attribute with where it is used and how far it is set up.

labels.description: What a person reads, by language; falls back to `name`
labels.title: Labels

variants_count.description: Entries that carry a value of it
variants_count.title: Variants Count

AttributeRow.title: AttributeRow

AttributeUpdate.description:
The name and the labels, always; the unit and the scale only while nothing is stored.

The key is not here: the readings and the rules name an attribute by it. A stored number
means what its unit says it means — `storage_mb` holds `16384` — and relabelling the
unit under it would make every stored value a different amount.
AttributeUpdate.title: AttributeUpdate

AxisCompare.description:
One identity axis, as the listing and the candidate each hold it.

`agrees` is null when one side has nothing on it: a silence, which the ladder treats
differently from a disagreement — and so should whoever is choosing.
AxisCompare.title: AxisCompare

BatchFailure.description:
One observation that did not go in, and why.

Named rather than counted: a batch reporting "two failed" is a batch nobody can fix.
BatchFailure.title: BatchFailure

BatchOffer.description: One observation inside a batch. The same thing as a single ingest, less the market.
BatchOffer.title: BatchOffer

BatchResult.description:
What a batch did, in the terms the run's own counters are kept in.

Partial on purpose. One malformed card in nine hundred should not throw away the pass
that collected the other eight hundred and ninety-nine — that is exactly the case
`runs.items_failed` exists to record.
BatchResult.title: BatchResult

BrandMatch.description: What a string resolves to. More than one row means the string is ambiguous.
BrandMatch.title: BrandMatch

BrandRef.description: A brand as a row names it: enough to print and to link, nothing to edit.
BrandRef.title: BrandRef

BrandRow.description:
A brand with how much of the catalogue it holds and how far it is set up.

`offers_count` counts new listings on sale placed on its entries, the rule the catalogue's
counts go by. A brand with no aliases resolves no shop's string; one with no products is
either new or left over from a merge, and both are worth finding.

models_count.description: Model names entered for it, in every category
models_count.title: Models Count

offers_count.description: New listings on sale placed on its entries
offers_count.title: Offers Count

BrandRow.title: BrandRow

Calibration.description:
Answers bucketed by the number their threshold is on, with what people said.

For a choice that number is `confidence`; for a model check it is the probability of
`same`, because that is what `JUDGE_DOUBT_BELOW` compares — a check that is sure the
listing is a sibling has high confidence and a `same` near nothing.
Calibration.title: Calibration

Candidate.description:
A near miss the matcher found while failing, and why it was considered.

A variant for the rungs that search entries; a brand for `brand_ambiguous`, whose
question is which maker a string means. `why` is the signal that found it — `gtin`,
`mpn`, `model`, `brand_alias` — and `axes` how it compares with the listing now, read
against the catalogue as it is rather than as it was when the row was written. There is
no score: the ladder does not rank, it agrees or refuses, and a number here would be one
invented for the page.

offers_count.description: Listings placed on this entry — how settled it is
offers_count.title: Offers Count

Candidate.title: Candidate

CategoryAliasCreate.description: A name a shop gives this category, in the language it gives it in.
CategoryAliasCreate.title: CategoryAliasCreate

CategoryAttributeCreate.description: Attaching an attribute to a category, and saying what it means there.
CategoryAttributeCreate.title: CategoryAttributeCreate

CategoryAttributeRead.description: An attribute bound to a category, the attribute named: a row can print `RAM`.
CategoryAttributeRead.title: CategoryAttributeRead

CategoryNode.description: A category in the tree, with its children and the totals of its whole branch.

offers_count.description: New listings on sale placed on its entries
offers_count.title: Offers Count

CategoryNode.title: CategoryNode

CategoryRow.description:
A category with how much of the catalogue it holds and how far it is set up.

Its own counts, not its branch's: `GET /categories/tree` adds the branch. `offers_count`
is new listings on sale placed on its entries, the catalogue's rule.

offers_count.description: New listings on sale placed on its entries
offers_count.title: Offers Count

CategoryRow.title: CategoryRow

CategoryUpdate.description:
Every field optional; only what is sent is applied.

`is_visible_effective` is not here — it is computed from the tree, and accepting it
would let a caller write a value the next recompute silently overrules.
CategoryUpdate.title: CategoryUpdate

ChannelSchedule.description:
One channel as the scheduler sees it: its schedule, its last run, its next slot.

The next slot is computed on read from the cron and never stored, for the reason `runs`
has no `next_run_at`: a stored one goes stale the moment somebody edits the schedule.
ChannelSchedule.title: ChannelSchedule

Check.description: One contract test and what it found.
Check.title: Check

CollectionHealth.description:
Whether a shop's collection is working, from its enabled channels' full passes.

`failing` when an enabled channel's newest full pass did not end ok — failed, rejected by
its contract, or interrupted; `never` when no enabled channel has finished one ok yet;
`ok` otherwise. A channel that is disabled says nothing about the shop's health.

failing_sources.description: Enabled channels whose newest full pass did not end ok
failing_sources.title: Failing Sources

last_full_ok_at.description: When the newest full pass that ended ok, on any channel, finished
last_full_ok_at.title: Last Full Ok At

CollectionHealth.title: CollectionHealth

CountryCreate.description:
Adding a country we have started to see shops from.

The seed carries only the markets we serve; the rest arrive this way rather than
through a migration, for the same reason a new market does — it is data, not a
release.
CountryCreate.title: CountryCreate

CountryUpdate.description:
Every field optional; only what is sent is applied.

The code is the identity and is not editable — a country that changes its ISO code is
a new row, not an edit.
CountryUpdate.title: CountryUpdate

Coverage.description:
How far a deterministic matcher could get on what has been read so far.

The number the whole design is downstream of. Everything after the matcher is shaped by
whether a barcode is usually there or almost never.
Coverage.title: Coverage

CreatedVariant.description: The entry a promotion makes. `id` is null on a dry run, which made nothing.
CreatedVariant.title: CreatedVariant

Decode.description:
How a response turns into fields.

The smallest part, and the one that changes without affecting anything else. Most
shops already publish machine-readable product data inside the page — for search
engines, or for their own front end — so reading markup is the fallback for the rest.
Decode.title: Decode

DismissalCreate.description: A word a shop writes for this attribute that is deliberately none of its values.
DismissalCreate.title: DismissalCreate

DoubtKept.description: A doubted match a person looked at and left where it was.
DoubtKept.title: DoubtKept

Due.description: A channel and kind the scheduler should start now.
Due.title: Due

Edge.description:
What passed from one node to the next. The difference to `source`'s count is what
stopped there.
Edge.title: Edge

EntrySnapshot.description:
A catalogue entry as it stood before the pair was tried. Null fields mean it was
already gone — folded into another by an earlier pair of the same pass.
EntrySnapshot.title: EntrySnapshot

ErrorResponse.description: Every non-2xx response from this API has this shape.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

Fact.description:
What a pass can bring back.

`catalogue` is everything matching stands on: barcodes, part numbers, model strings,
attributes. The other two are observations about one listing at one moment.
Fact.title: Fact

IngestResult.description:
What the observation did.

`stored` is false when the content hashed to something already on file: an unchanged
page bumps a timestamp and writes nothing, which is what keeps the raw table
proportional to how much the world changes rather than how often we look.
IngestResult.title: IngestResult

ItemFailure.description:
One product that did not make it into the run, and where it broke.

`fetch`: its page could not be read. `parse`: the page was read and the channel's parser
raised on it — the bytes are in the snapshot store's `failed/` area, which is what makes
it a five-minute fix. `ingest`: parsed, and refused by the service when handed over.
ItemFailure.title: ItemFailure

Job.description:
Everything a collector needs to do one run.

Asked for rather than passed on a command line: the channel's declaration comes with
it, because a worker has to know whether this pass is the full one or the cheap one,
and which facts the cheap one is expected to bring back.
Job.title: Job

JudgeConfig.description: Whether the judge can be asked at all, and the numbers its answers are read by.
JudgeConfig.title: JudgeConfig

JudgeReport.description:
What a pass over the queue did, in the terms that decide whether to run it again.

`asked` is what was paid for and `cached` is what was not, so the two together say
whether the store is earning its keep.
JudgeReport.title: JudgeReport

JudgeWindow.description:
What the judge cost over one stretch of time.

`asked` and the tokens are the answers bought — one stored verdict each, so they are
exact. `cached` is how many questions were answered from the store instead, summed from
the passes' own reports in the audit trail: a cache hit writes no verdict, and the
trail is the one place it is recorded. No money: the price per token is the provider's
and changes, and a figure computed from a stale one would be believed.
JudgeWindow.title: JudgeWindow

ManualMatch.description: A human placing a listing themselves.
ManualMatch.title: ManualMatch

MarketCreate.description:
Opening a storefront. Disabled unless asked otherwise: a market is created, wired
into the parsers, mapped, and only then shown.
MarketCreate.title: MarketCreate

offers_count.description: Listings on sale in it now, from the shops shown there
offers_count.title: Offers Count

products_count.description: Visible families with a new listing on sale in it from a shown shop
products_count.title: Products Count

shops_attached.description: Shops attached to it, shown or not
shops_attached.title: Shops Attached

MarketState.description: Where a shop stands in one market, for `?market_code=`.
MarketState.title: MarketState

MarketUpdate.description:
Every field optional; only what is sent is applied.

The code is the identity and is not editable — a market in another country is
another market.
MarketUpdate.title: MarketUpdate

MatchDoubtRead.description:
A match a rule made that the judge doubts, with what it was shown and what it said.

Read-only on purpose. A doubt is a question for a person — unlink, split, merge or
leave — and never a reason for the matcher to move a listing by itself.
MatchDoubtRead.title: MatchDoubtRead

MatchOutcome.description: What running the matcher over one listing did.
MatchOutcome.title: MatchOutcome

MatchQueueRead.description:
A listing the matcher could not place, with the listing itself and what it found.

`brand` and `model_key` are what it looked for; `siblings` counts the queued listings
looking for the same brand and model — what one new entry would place.
MatchQueueRead.title: MatchQueueRead

MatchState.description:
Where the matcher left a listing. `queued` holds the ambiguous ones too — which kind
of stuck it is, is the queue's `reason`.
MatchState.title: MatchState

MergePair.description:
Two entries one barcode named, and what became of them.

`from` is folded in and disappears, `into` survives. A refused pair is the one worth
reading: one barcode on two brands or two categories is more often an error in a shop's
data than two products.
MergePair.title: MergePair

MergeReport.description:
What a pass of merges did.

A barcode is the strongest thing this system has, so two catalogue entries both holding
listings that carry one and the same barcode are not two products. `refused` is the
interesting number: a pair the barcode named and something else contradicted.
MergeReport.title: MergeReport

Method.description:
Which rung of the ladder fired.

Kept because trust in them differs wildly: a barcode is proof, a model string that
happened to agree is a guess that landed.
Method.title: Method

ModelAliasCreate.description:
One way a shop writes a model, and the spelling the catalogue uses for it.

`alias` is what is found in a title; `model` is what the reading comes out as. Adding
the canonical spelling as an alias of itself is the usual first row, and the one the
seed writes — a name that is only a target is never found.
ModelAliasCreate.title: ModelAliasCreate

OfferBrief.description: The listing a queue row or a doubt is about, enough to decide from the row.
OfferBrief.title: OfferBrief

OfferRead.description:
One listing, with the shop that has it and where the catalogue placed it.

`listed` is whether the shop still has it: seen by its channel's newest full pass that
ended ok. A listing the shop took down keeps its history and its last price, which is
no longer a price anybody can pay.

brand.description: The placed product's brand; null unplaced

brand_raw.description: The brand as the shop wrote it
brand_raw.title: Brand Raw

category.description: The placed product's category, else what the channel collects

title.description: As the shop wrote it, from its newest full pass
title.title: Title

OfferRead.title: OfferRead

OfferTrace.description:
One listing from the shop's bytes to the catalogue, step by step.

`now` is the reading recomputed with today's rules and words, with `steps` saying how it
was reached; `stored` is what the database holds. They differ when a rule or the registry
changed since the listing was last read, which is what `stale` says.
OfferTrace.title: OfferTrace

PasswordChange.description: Changing your own password. Proving the current one is what makes it yours.
PasswordChange.title: PasswordChange

PasswordReset.description:
An administrator setting another account's password: a colleague who lost theirs, or a
collector's machine account. No current password — the caller is not the owner, and the
admin token is what authorises it.
PasswordReset.title: PasswordReset

PendingKind.description:
What a pass of one kind would pay for if started now.

`eligible` is every listing it would consider with no limit; `to_ask` the distinct
questions among them the store has no answer for — two shops writing one title are one
question. The tokens are that times this kind's average so far, null before any answer
of the kind was bought.
PendingKind.title: PendingKind

Pipeline.description: The pipeline for one category, one channel or everything, with the channels under it.
Pipeline.title: Pipeline

PipelineDay.description:
The pipeline's key numbers as they stood on one day. Missing days were not kept —
the scheduler was not running — and cannot be recomputed.
PipelineDay.title: PipelineDay

PlacedOn.description: The catalogue entry a listing is placed on, and by what signal.
PlacedOn.title: PlacedOn

ProductRead.description:
A family, with what a list of them needs to be read without further requests.

The brand and the category come named, so a table shows `Lenovo` rather than `#15`, and
three counts say whether the family is comparable at all: how many entries it holds,
how many listings on sale new are placed on them and at how many shops, and the lowest
price any of them asks.

min_price.description: The lowest price of those listings, in the shop's currency (EUR)
min_price.title: Min Price

offers_count.description: New listings on sale placed on one of them
offers_count.title: Offers Count

ProductRead.title: ProductRead

ProductRef.description: The family an entry belongs to.
ProductRef.title: ProductRef

ProductUpdate.description:
`title` and `slug` are absent on purpose — both are derived.

A generated title is corrected through `title_override`, which survives the next
regeneration. Accepting the title itself would let a caller write a value the next
model change silently overwrites.
ProductUpdate.title: ProductUpdate

PromotionReport.description:
What a pass of promotions did.

`matched` is the interesting number: a listing that turned out to match a variant made
moments earlier, from another shop's listing of the same product. It is the whole point
of the exercise, and it is why a sweep tries to match before it promotes.
PromotionReport.title: PromotionReport

QueueSummary.description:
The breakdown that answers what to build next.

If most listings sit in `signals_unmatched`, the work is creating variants. In
`brand_unknown`, it is reading raw strings and naming the brand behind them. In
`brand_ambiguous` or `ambiguous`, the candidates are already there and the work is
choosing — the two buckets a judge can help with, and if both are nearly empty, a judge
is not what this needs. In `no_signals`, it is pulling identity out of titles.
QueueSummary.title: QueueSummary

RawOfferBatch.description:
Many observations of one channel, in one request.

One at a time, a full pass of a nine-hundred-product shop is nine hundred requests,
nine hundred transactions and nine hundred audit entries — and that last one is the
real objection: the trail exists to show what an administrator did, and a crawl would
bury that under a wall of "an offer arrived".

Post it gzipped. Product JSON compresses by roughly an order of magnitude, and the
difference is paid on every pass of every channel.
RawOfferBatch.title: RawOfferBatch

RawOfferIngest.description:
One observation, as a fetcher would submit it.

The payload is stored verbatim — this is the only place in the system where bytes from
outside are kept as they arrived, and everything downstream is derived from it.
RawOfferIngest.title: RawOfferIngest

Reason.description:
Why a listing could not be placed.

Seven different problems that route to seven different kinds of work. One
undifferentiated pile is a pile nobody sorts — and a pile that says `ambiguous` when
nothing can settle it is worse than undifferentiated, because it sends somebody to
choose with nothing to choose from.
Reason.title: Reason

RenameReport.description:
What a pass of rebuilds did.

A catalogue entry made from one listing is named after that listing's reading. When the
reading improves — a rule fixed, a word entered in the registry — the entry keeps the
old name and nothing goes back for it. `merged` is the good outcome: renamed, the entry
turned out to be one that already existed.
RenameReport.title: RenameReport

RunBrief.description: A channel's newest run, as a list row shows it.
RunBrief.title: RunBrief

RunContract.description:
The contract's verdict and every check behind it. `not_evaluated` for a run that
broke, or has not finished: judging the counts of a crash is judging nothing.
RunContract.title: RunContract

RunFailures.description: The sample a run kept of what did not make it, beside how many did not.
RunFailures.title: RunFailures

RunFlow.description:
One run through the same nodes, filling in while it runs.

The first half is what the worker reported (`progress`): how many product pages it found,
read and handed over. The second half is counted from the tables: what became of the
listings this run saw, and what settling it placed. Both are there as the run goes, so a
page polling this watches the nodes fill in order.
RunFlow.title: RunFlow

RunProgress.description: What a worker has done so far. Counts only; each report replaces the last one's.
RunProgress.title: RunProgress

RunProgressRead.description:
What a run has done so far: the worker's counts while it reads, then what settling
it placed. `phase` walks `reading` → `settling` → `settled` (or `unsettled`, with the
reason); a quick pass ends at `done`.
RunProgressRead.title: RunProgressRead

RunRead.description: One run, named: which channel, of which shop, collecting what.

coverage.description: Share of handed-over listings carrying each field: {field: 0..1}
coverage.title: Coverage

duration_seconds.description: From start to finish; null while it is live
duration_seconds.title: Duration Seconds

RunRead.title: RunRead

RunResult.description: What a worker reports back when it is done.
RunResult.title: RunResult

SchedulerStatus.description:
Whether the scheduler is alive, and what it is doing and will do.

`alive` is a heartbeat fresher than three ticks. Nothing else can say it: a scheduler
with nothing due is as quiet as one that has stopped.

progress.description: Running run id → listings of its channel seen since it started
progress.title: Progress

SchedulerStatus.title: SchedulerStatus

SellerRef.description: Who sells it within the shop: the shop itself, or a trader on a marketplace.
SellerRef.title: SellerRef

hidden_markets.description: The markets it is attached to and not shown in
hidden_markets.title: Hidden Markets

markets.description: The markets it is shown in
markets.title: Markets

offers_count.description: Its listings on sale now, of any condition
offers_count.title: Offers Count

ShopRead.title: ShopRead

SourceFlow.description: One channel's own pass through the same nodes.
SourceFlow.title: SourceFlow

SourceRead.description: A channel, with its newest run, its next slots and what it has on sale now.

last_full_ok_at.description: When its newest full pass that ended ok finished
last_full_ok_at.title: Last Full Ok At

next_full_at.description: Its next scheduled full pass; none while disabled
next_full_at.title: Next Full At

SourceRead.title: SourceRead

Stage.description: One node: how many things reached it, and what they are made of.
Stage.title: Stage

TraceCandidate.description:
A near miss as the queue row stored it, named. Compared axis by axis with the
listing in `GET /api/admin/match-queue/{offer_id}`, which is where the choosing is.
TraceCandidate.title: TraceCandidate

TraceEntry.description: The catalogue entry the listing is on, and who else is.
TraceEntry.title: TraceEntry

TraceObservation.description: What the shop served, as the channel parsed it — the newest pass that carried it.
TraceObservation.title: TraceObservation

TraceStep.description: One rule as it ran on this listing, and exactly what it changed.
TraceStep.title: TraceStep

Trust.description: How much the channel's data is worth, not how good the shop is.
Trust.title: Trust

UnresolvedReason.description:
Why a listing's colour field left its reading without a colour.

`unknown`: the registry has no word for what the shop wrote — a row to enter. `pair`: it
knows each colour and not the combination. `conflict`:
every field resolves, to different colours, and the reading takes none of them, as it
should; no alias fixes that. `resolves_now`: the fields agree under the registry as it is
today and the stored reading is older — a reparse fills it.
UnresolvedReason.title: UnresolvedReason

UnresolvedReport.description:
The listings with a colour field and no colour in their reading, and why.

Computed from the current readings with the registry as it is now, so it is never stale
and stores nothing; a listing with no colour field at all is not here — that colour is
in its title, which is the judge's.
UnresolvedReport.title: UnresolvedReport

UnresolvedValue.description: One thing shops write in a colour field, and why it did not become a colour.

conflicts_with.description: The other fields' colours, for a conflict
conflicts_with.title: Conflicts With

get.description:
The number everything else in the parser design is downstream of.

A barcode is the strongest signal, brand with a part number the next, a brand alone
narrows the field but decides nothing. If most readings land in the last bucket, the
centre of the work is pulling identity out of free text rather than matching.

Each value with its reason: `unknown` is a word to enter in the registry,
`conflict` fields that name different colours — which the reading rightly refuses,
and no alias fixes — and `resolves_now` a reading older than the registry, which a
reparse fills. Mark a word that is none of the colours with
`POST /api/admin/attributes/{attribute_id}/dismissals`.
